key_insight: Coding agents can autonomously compress LLMs, with the best design per task averaging a 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16.
engineering_relevance: Agent-driven compression can reduce model storage while preserving much of baseline performance, but requires independent inference and capability checks.
method: Give agents a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget.
Let agents design compressed weights and inference code using perplexity-guided experiments.
Independently verify final models and evaluate downstream accuracy.
evidence_signal: Across six agents and six model–size settings, 29 of 36 submissions passed verification; the best-perplexity designs achieved 77.33% downstream accuracy versus 79.56% for BF16.
watch_item: Local perplexity gains may not transfer to complete models, and likelihood alone can miss generation and inference failures.
paper_title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
